tasks.title: Random wind, weight and sensor noise
tasks.desc: So a policy trained in the simulator does not depend on its perfect physics.

tasks.title: Match the simulated motors to the real ones

notes.text: Question: The simulator uses the spec sheet's 900 g of thrust per motor. Can you weigh the real thrust on a kitchen scale? Cheap motors often fall 10-20% short, and a policy trained on thrust it does not have will crash in gusts.

tasks.title: Reward for passing gates without crashing

notes.text: Points for each gate, a penalty for crashing and a small one for battery use.

tasks.title: Train the first policy
tasks.desc:
A policy that flies the drone from its camera and motion sensors alone.

- [x] Passes every gate on most random courses
- [x] Copes with wind up to 8 m/s

notes.text: Plan: PPO on 64 simulators at once, overnight.

The policy flies the course on its own: 92 of 100 random courses through every gate, 3 crashes, 5 too slow.

**Check:** `make replay` plays ten flights, the three crashes among them; all three happen in gusts above 7 m/s.

**Decide:** good enough to try on the real drone in calm weather, or train on stronger wind first (about 6 more hours)?

tasks.title: Hold steady in strong gusts
tasks.desc: Keep training the first policy on gusts up to 12 m/s, with the measured motors; about 6 hours.

tasks.title: Run the policy on the drone's computer
tasks.desc: Export it for the onboard computer and check it decides 50 times a second.

tasks.title: 100 test courses kept out of training
tasks.desc: Fixed seeds, so every policy flies exactly the same courses and wind in the simulator.

tasks.title: Simulator race against the hand-tuned autopilot
